newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan 96 platinum demand to dip 3.4% - bullion house.
newsitem.headline: Japan 96 platinum demand to dip 3.4% - bullion house.

text.p: Platinum demand in Japan in calendar 1996 is expected to fall 3.4 percent to 70.0 tonnes from last year's 72.5 tonnes, Japan's largest bullion house said in a report.

An official at Tanaka Kikinzoku Kogyo KK blamed the decline largely on sluggish investor demand for bars and other forms of physical platinum. Such demand was forecast to slip to 4.5 tonnes, compared with 9.5 tonnes last year.
He attributed waning investor purchases to a weaker yen against the dollar, which lifted yen-based retail prices.
Tanaka expected Japan's platinum jewellery consumption to be flat at 46.0 tonnes, while seeing use in auto catalysts at 8.0 tonnes, off modestly from last year's 8.4 tonnes.
It forecast platinum imports at 68.0 tonnes, down from the previous year's 70.5 tonnes.
On the global outlook, it expected a platinum surplus of 7.5 tonnes in 1996, up from last year's 6.0 tonne surplus.

Global platinum supplies were seen rising to 157.5 tonnes from 154.9 tonnes, backed by a slight increase in supplies from South Africa and Russia. It forecast global platinum demand at 150.0 tonnes in 1996, compared with last year's 148.9 tonnes.
